question: Risks to individuals and society emerge when young adults disconnect from the labour market. In December 2023, in the European Union, 2.86 million young people (under 25) were unemployed, with 2.32 million of these in the euro area, according to Eurostat. Compared with December 2022, youth unemployment had increased by 102 000 in the EU and 84 000 in the euro area. In this context: 1.

Can the Commission provide a comprehensive update on the progress made in the current youth employment initiatives in Member States afflicted with high rates of youth unemployment, including any adjustments implemented to improve their efficiency?

Given the disparity between current figures and the ambitious target of reducing the unemployment rate among young people (aged 15–29) to 9 % by 2030, as specified in the European Pillar of Social Rights action plan, what measures does the Commission intend to adopt to accomplish this goal?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.4.2024) A key aim of the European Pillar of Social Rights action plan is to improve the employability of young people. In this regard, the reinforced Youth Guarantee1 provides guidance for stable labour market integration, with a focus on quality employment, for young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEETs).

The Commission with the Employment Committee are monitoring the implementation of the Youth Guarantee on a biannual basis. The last review (2023) showed that Member States maintained a strong political commitment for implementing the Youth Guarantee and most of them are making efforts to improve the delivery of services to NEETs.

But challenges and substantial differences remain in the quality and effectiveness of service delivery, while preventive and outreach measures should be strengthened in particular for the most vulnerable NEETs.

In addition to the Youth Guarantee, the Commission has been supporting young people through many initiatives including, on (up)-skilling, recognition of qualifications and quality frameworks for traineeships and apprenticeships. On 20 March 2024, the Commission proposed a new initiative reinforcing the quality of traineeships.

Young people have also been at the heart of the 2022 European Year of Youth and the ongoing European Year of Skills. Finally, in 2021-2027, around EUR 23 billion will be invested under EU funds to support young people. The Commission is committed to continue the efforts to ensure that no young person is left behind.
